title: Key the wait ledger on test block and call position, not line number

Each row now names its call by file, the exact description of its enclosing `test_that()` block (or the top-level function in `helper-parallel.R`), and the call's position among that block's wait calls. Both accounting guards and the explicit-bound re-read use that key, and `DECLARED_UNCHECKABLE_BOUNDS` is keyed the same way. Renaming a test in a budgeted file, or adding, removing or reordering a wait call in it, means editing its rows; the guards fail and name the row until that is done.

The bounds and per-file totals are unchanged. Probes run on a scratch copy: a blank line atop all 8 ledger files passes; deleting each of the 95 budgeted rows fails with that row's key in the message; doubling each of the 10 copied bounds fails that row's bound check. `devtools::check()`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.

A manual stress run on macOS (run 39378513433) installed everything from CRAN and passed.

title: Seed checks in the refusal tests can fail
description:
Test-only change, plus one source comment. No package behavior changes.

Several tests claimed that a refusal fires before the RNG is drawn, and backed the claim with `expect_identical(.Random.seed, before)`. That comparison cannot fail there: the function registers `restore_rng()` before its draw, so a seed the caller set comes back either way. These tests now remove the generator state, call the function, and assert that no state exists afterwards. This fails when the draw comes first, because a session with no state keeps the one a draw creates. A new test helper, `local_no_rng_state()`, does the removal and puts the state back when the block exits.

- The refusal blocks in `test-event-level.R`, `test-nested-final-fit-resamples.R`, `test-nested-final-fit-set.R` and `test-nested-final-fit-identity.R` (including the `expect_mismatch()` helper), and the two existing blocks in `test-nested-final-fit-checks.R`, use the helper.

- The block "the record refusals fire before anything is drawn" triggered one refusal. It is renamed to name that refusal.
- The comment above `check_workflow_identity()` in `R/nested-final-fit.R` now gives the reason for the order correctly.

The four `expect_identical(.Random.seed, before)` comparisons that remain were each checked against a planted break (the restore removed, or a draw added) and fail under it.

A regression test in `test-nested-tune-finalize.R` fails 4 times without the fix and passes with it.

title: Frame the inner splits on the analysis set under a repeated outer row
description:
When an outer split repeats a row in its in_id, each inner tuning call now gets its inner splits on the outer fold's analysis set, as it already did for designs without repeats. tune therefore finalizes an unknown parameter range (for example a min_n() finalized by row count) without the outer fold's held-out rows.

- Inner indices map onto the analysis frame by occurrence: the r-th mention of a row goes to its r-th copy, cycling past the last copy. Without repeats this is match(), as before.
- An inner assessment set left as the complement holds every copy the outer split holds of each row the inner split does not train on, and no outer held-out row.
- When the inner splits must stay on the whole frame (an outer in_id with an NA, fractional, below-1 or past-the-data index, or an inner split that cannot be placed), each derivable logical NA out_id is still made explicit as the outer rows of its complement, with or without repeats.
- Tests: oracle tests for the finalized range and against an analysis-frame reference design, plus tests for the mapping, the complement, the whole-frame paths and RNG use.
- NEWS, the help for the nested tuning functions and the design notes are updated.

title: Keep a renamed apparent split out of a bootstrap design
description:
An apparent split beside bootstrap or permutation splits now counts as part of that design only if its id is "Apparent", the one split tune leaves out of its estimates. Under any other id, tune scores the split on the rows it trained on, so nestedtune now refuses it as an `apparent()` split in both loops.

title: Refuse an inner "Apparent" split that tune drops or a race misreads

This change adds two inner-loop refusals with class `nestedtune_bad_design`:

- A split whose id is "Apparent" is refused, unless it is the apparent split of a bootstrap design (`bootstraps()` or `group_bootstraps()` with `apparent = TRUE`).
- `nested_tune_race_anova()` and `nested_tune_race_win_loss()` also refuse that bootstrap apparent split. `nested_workflow_map()` refuses it before any workflow runs, if a workflow routes to a racer.

`check_nested()` and `nested_resamples()` apply both rules. `nested_final_fit()` applies them to the inner design it rebuilds on all the data. title: Averaged out-of-fold predictions: collect_predictions(summarize = TRUE)
description:
`collect_predictions()` on a nested result or a workflow-set result gains `summarize`, which defaults to `FALSE`. With `summarize = TRUE` it returns one averaged prediction per data row, taken over every completed outer fold that held the row out.

- The rules are tune's for `summarize = TRUE`. Numeric predictions take the mean with missing values ignored. Class probabilities are averaged and renormalized, and the class is recomputed from them. A class-only run takes the most frequent class. A censored run takes the median `.pred_time` and the mean survival per `.eval_time`. Ties go to the first level.
- Each fold selected its own candidate, so the average spans those candidates, and the fold labels and `.config` are dropped.
- A row whose averaged probabilities are all missing gets a missing class, where tune gives it the first level. The help page states this difference.
- Quantile predictions are refused with class `nestedtune_summarize_quantile`.
- A run with failed folds averages the completed folds and warns once.

Tests compare the average with `tune::collect_predictions(summarize = TRUE)` on `tune::fit_resamples()` over the same outer splits for regression, probability, class-only and censored runs. They also compare it with a base R computation on grid runs whose repeats selected different candidates. `devtools::check()` gives 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes locally.

- On a design that holds each row out once, the saved predictions are joined as they are, unchanged from before.
- A design that leaves some row out of every assessment set is still refused with class `nestedtune_augment_rows`. The message names the first five such rows and no design type.

The help page and NEWS.md state the change. `devtools::check()`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.

title: Edge cases of averaged predictions
description:
`collect_predictions(summarize = TRUE)` and `augment()` now refuse, by name, saved-prediction tables their shared average would misread:

- `collect_predictions(summarize = TRUE)` runs the row check that `augment()` and `compute_metrics()` run, with class `nestedtune_collect_predictions_predictions`. The per-fold table is not checked.
- Both averaging readers refuse, with class `nestedtune_summarize_columns`, two or more factor outcome columns, a `.pred_class` with no factor outcome, and a censored `.pred` entry that is not `NULL` and has no `.eval_time`.
- A `NULL` censored entry is left out of its row's average, and a row with no other entry holds `NULL`.
- `augment()` checks a name collision before any refusal of the average.
- The average is rewritten with grouped sums and `mean()`'s second pass. On `benchmarks/averaging-speed.R`'s 100,002-row probability table it runs at 0.090 of the previous time, and its output agrees with a frozen copy of the previous code.

Both help pages now say that a metric computed on averaged predictions describes an average of several fitted models, not the nested estimate, and name `collect_metrics()` for that estimate.

title: Stop five messages breaking across two lines mid-sentence
description:
Five messages were written as one string continued onto a second source line with a trailing backslash. `cli_abort()`, `cli_warn()`, `cli_bullets()` and `cli_text()` join such a line, but `cli::format_inline()` does not: it keeps the newline and the indent, and with glue braces in the string it keeps the backslash too. So each of these reached the reader broken partway through a sentence.

The refusal `nested_final_fit()` gives for reordered model arguments read:

```
The model's arguments differ: recorded in the order "a" and "b", given in the order \
       "b" and "a".
```

The other four are three refusals of a malformed nested design and the completion line of a workflow set's print. Each string is now two pieces joined with `paste()`. The forty-odd other continuations in the package reach one of the functions that join them and are left alone; each callee was checked directly.

`tests/testthat/test-format-inline.R` renders the reordered-arguments refusal and asserts it holds no backslash and no newline, and statically parses every file in `R/` for a continued string inside a `format_inline()` call. Before the fix the guard named exactly the five sites; after it, none. It skips when `R/` is not in the tree, as this repo's other source-scanning tests do.

Suite clean at 10,582 passes.

title: Readers tune users expect: final-fit extractors, wide metrics, plot filters, predict refusal

The generics are re-exported beside `extract_workflow()`, and the methods refuse an argument they do not know.

`collect_metrics()` on a `nested_results` or a `nested_results_set` takes `type = "wide"`: one column per metric, keyed on the fold labels, `.eval_time` and `wflow_id`. A metric scored with two estimators, or named like a key column, is refused with class `nestedtune_wide_collision` rather than overwritten.

`autoplot(type = "performance")` on both classes takes `metric` and `eval_time` to choose panels. A static metric's panel is kept whatever `eval_time` names, as in tune. A metric or time the run did not score, or either argument with the parameters view, is refused with class `nestedtune_bad_plot_filter`.

`predict()` on a `nested_results` or a `nested_results_set` refuses with class `nestedtune_predict_results` and names `nested_final_fit()`, where R gave its generic "no applicable method" before.

title: Model specification with a formula or recipe as the orchestrators' input
description:
The six orchestrators (`nested_tune_grid()`, `nested_tune_bayes()`, `nested_tune_race_anova()`, `nested_tune_race_win_loss()`, `nested_tune_sim_anneal()` and `nested_fit_resamples()`) now take a parsnip model specification with a formula or a recipe, in tune's argument order:

```r
nested_tune_grid(spec, preprocessor, resamples)
```

Each function is now an S3 generic with `workflow`, `model_spec` and `default` methods. The `workflow` method keeps the current signature. The `model_spec` method wraps the two in `workflows::workflow(preprocessor, spec)` and runs the workflow path. Under the same seed, the result is identical to the call on that workflow.

The refusals have classes. A missing or wrong preprocessor raises `nestedtune_bad_preprocessor`. A preprocessor given beside a workflow raises `nestedtune_preprocessor_with_workflow`. A missing `resamples` or `object` is refused with an error that names the function called. `nested_final_fit()` still takes a workflow, and its message for a bare specification names the wrapping.

title: Rolling-origin and sliding-window outer designs

title: Take P3M binaries on macOS too, working around the zstd extraction failure
description:
The macOS check leg cannot install dependencies. CRAN has begun compressing its macOS binaries with zstd under the `.tgz` name, and the `pak` that `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2` installs cannot extract them:

```
Cannot extract '.../sonoma-arm64/contrib/4.6/censored_0.3.5.tgz', unknown archive type.
```

`censored` is one of this package's Suggests, so every macOS run hits it. It failed twice in 55 seconds on #118, whose diff is three lines inside one `deparse()` call, and every check run through 2026-09-17 passed. Upstream: https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/issues/485, where the maintainer gives taking P3M's binaries as the workaround.

This repo had deliberately excluded macOS from P3M, because P3M's macOS binaries link OpenMP and the runners ship no libomp, which made `gower` fail to load. That package is still built from source on macOS by the existing `gower?source` entry, so its own failure stays fixed. The rewritten comment records both failure modes and says to revert this once pkgdepends reads zstd.

No package file changes; the local suite is clean at 10,576 passes.

Every leaf of the identity goes through one `deparse()` call, so the option is pinned there for the duration of the call and restored on exit.

The regression test records the identity of a workflow with `penalty = 1e5`, sets `options(scipen = 100)`, and asserts the identity is unchanged. It fails before the fix on `"100000"` against `"1e+05"` and passes after it. Its control asserts the recorded form is `1e+05`, so a pin that made both sides print long would not satisfy it.

title: The prose sweep reads as prose only what its definition names
description:
`benchmarks/sweep-prose.R` states which lines of a page are not prose, but its parser did not implement that definition. Nine paragraphs over the six pages came from those leaks.

`rmd_paragraphs()` now implements the stated partition: a badge line goes in every mode, a fence line is matched with leading whitespace or without, an HTML comment drops from its opening line through the line holding `-->`, and a list item, bulleted or numbered, takes the lines it wraps onto up to the next blank line. The script header is rewritten to state that partition.

Two further rules keep the parse from going quiet over a page rather than leaking into it. An opener with no `-->` under it closes nothing and drops its own line alone, so a typo cannot empty a page of the prose a sweep would read. The list-item loop skips lines the parser already dropped, so an item-shaped line inside the YAML header or a fenced chunk opens no run.

A hand-authored fixture plants one leak per rule, and two `test_that()` blocks cover them. No page prose changed: the six gating sweeps print `clean` and exit 0, `devtools::test()` passes 9854, and `devtools::check()` returns 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.

title: The coverage job survives a daemon killed while writing its trace
description:
The test-coverage job failed intermittently with `Error in readRDS(f) : error reading from connection` inside covr's merge, after every test passed. The failed run's artifact shows why: the four test-worker trace files are whole, and three daemon trace files are truncated at a page boundary. A daemon started by the suite loads the instrumented package and writes its trace in an exit finalizer, and nothing waits for that write: `mirai::daemons(0)` only asks daemons to exit, and processx kills a worker's children when testthat shuts the worker down.

The fix: under covr, `tests/testthat/helper-covr.R` points `COVERAGE_DIR` at a `daemon-traces` sidecar directory, so the workers and every daemon they spawn write there. `test-coverage.yaml` merges the sidecar afterwards with covr's own merge and skips any file that cannot be read, so a killed daemon costs its own counts and not the job. Checked against the failed run's trace files: three skipped, the rest merged.

Regression tests in `tests/testthat/test-covr-traces.R` fail on main and pass here; the full suite is clean.

title: M076: price the two test-suite levers, and set the check-step caps from measurement
description:
Rebalances nothing, and says why in numbers.

M74's re-cut left two test-suite levers unpriced: splitting
`test-parallel-identity.R` at its daemon-pool boundaries, and re-ordering
`Config/testthat/start-first` by measured per-file time. Both were
implemented and both were reverted on the measurement.

At four workers, the count the ubuntu and windows runners use:

| configuration | sum of per-file wall | ÷ 4 workers | wall clock, median (range) |
|---|---|---|---|
| branch point | 777.6 s | 194.4 s | **198.0 s** (196.6-199.4) |
| reorder only | 794.8 s | 198.7 s | 202.8 s (201.9-205.3) |
| split only | 862.1 s | 215.5 s | 220.1 s (191.6-239.4) |
| split + reorder | 789.9 s | 197.5 s | 201.1 s (185.0-203.2) |

The `÷ 4 workers` column is the floor a perfect packing of that
configuration's own work could reach. The branch point runs 1.9% above its
floor, so the queue is already almost fully packed and a re-ordering has
nothing to recover. The split is worse than neutral: it adds work, three
daemon-pool starts and three worker package-loads where there was one, and a
4-vCPU runner pays that more than the 18-core machine these figures came
from.

What the branch keeps is `benchmarks/profile-tests-parallel.R`, the parallel
counterpart to the serial `benchmarks/profile-tests.R`, and
`benchmarks/test-timing-parallel.md` holding the table above. Both are
`.Rbuildignore`d, so the package `R CMD check` sees here is byte-identical to
the default branch.

Still to come on this branch: three timings of the `check-r-package` step per
leg on one head, and each leg's `timeout-minutes` set from its median.

Prunes the test suite so each claim is asserted once, and dispositions the nine files that test the harness or a repo artifact rather than the package.

- 15 duplicate `test_that()` blocks removed, each with its surviving partner named in the milestone's removal table; partners that asserted less were extended rather than kept alongside.
- `test-vignette-citations.R` and `test-drift-manifest.R` deleted (repo-artifact tests with no default-branch defect behind them), along with `helper-drift-manifest.R`.
- `test-fixture-cache.R` and `test-hang-trace.R` trimmed to the blocks that fail on a defect in the harness the suite depends on.
- `test-suite-hygiene.R`, `test-ci-workflows.R`, `test-dots-barrier.R` and `test-control-slots.R` kept whole; `test-parallel-classify.R` read as package tests and only deduplicated.
- Two helpers the deletions left uncalled removed.

Block count 795 -> 749. `devtools::test()` 0 failures, 0 skips; `devtools::check()` 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.

title: M72: summary(), autoplot() and agreement() on a nested_results_set
description:
Gives the three single-workflow readers a `nested_results_set` method, each workflow's view keyed by its `wflow_id`:

- `summary()` returns a list of per-workflow summaries with one h1 and one h2 per workflow.
- `autoplot(type = "performance")` puts workflows on the x axis inside metric panels with a rule per workflow at its mean; `autoplot(type = "parameters")` draws one panel per (workflow, tuned parameter) over a pooled axis.
- `agreement()` stacks each element's table under `wflow_id`.
- Fold-state rules (partial warning, all-failed empty slot, no-completed refusal) on both views; help page, pkgdown row, NEWS bullet, `tuners.Rmd` set section.

Tracking: `cairn/milestones/M72-set-readers.md`.

title: M73: a nested_results_set keeps its class only while every row is one of the run's own workflows, and a re-signalled condition keeps its original's fields
description:
One reconstruction rule for `nested_results_set`, routed to from five doors (`dplyr_reconstruct()`, `[`, `vec_restore()`, base `rbind()`, `names<-`): the class and `fn` attribute survive an operation exactly when every row left is one of the run's own workflows, with no repeated `wflow_id`, no record column dropped or renamed, and at least one row; otherwise a plain tibble comes back. The readers, `summary()`, `print()`, `extract_workflow()` and `nested_final_fit()` answer on a kept subset for the rows in hand. `resignal_for_workflow()` re-raises the original condition object with the workflow id prefixed to its first message line, keeping its class vector, parent, bullets and data fields.

Help-page section, NEWS bullet and DESIGN sentence document which operations keep the class. D-059 records the rule.

Milestone record: `cairn/milestones/M73-set-invariants.md`.

title: M68: save_pred and extract reach the outer fit; collect_predictions() and collect_extracts() stack what each fold kept
description:
When the control passed through `...` carries `save_pred = TRUE` or an `extract` function, each outer fold keeps the assessment-set predictions and the extract of the fitted workflow from its scoring fit, as `.predictions` and `.extracts` list columns on the `nested_results`. A failed fold holds `NULL` in each; an extract that errors leaves the fold completed with a `NULL` and an `"outer extract"` note. Both columns are record columns under the dplyr and vctrs invariant. `collect_predictions()` and `collect_extracts()` gain `nested_results` methods on tune's generics, stacking the completed folds with the recorded label columns first, and refusing an object lacking the column with a classed condition naming the control slot.

Help text on the four orchestrator pages, a `collect_predictions.nested_results` topic, pkgdown row, NEWS entry, DESIGN Function Families line, and a `results.Rmd` paragraph. D-054 records the decision.

Tracking: `cairn/milestones/M68-outer-predictions.md`.

title: M69: a `select` argument on the five orchestrators takes a `selection_rule()`, and the final fit applies the recorded rule
description:
## Summary

- New exported constructor `selection_rule(rule = c("best", "one_std_err", "pct_loss"), ..., limit = NULL)` holding the rule name, the parameter orderings as bare expressions, and `limit` (default 2 for `pct_loss` only).
- A `select = selection_rule("best")` argument on `nested_tune_grid()`, `nested_tune_bayes()`, `nested_tune_race_anova()`, `nested_tune_race_win_loss()` and `nested_tune_sim_anneal()`, checked at entry (`nestedtune_bad_selection_rule`, `nestedtune_selection_rule_unknown_param`), sent with each fold, and applied in `nested_fold_fit()` through tune's three selectors.
- The rule joins the `procedure` record as `select`; `nested_final_fit()` applies the recorded rule, and refuses a record lacking one.
- BC15 parallel-identity block under `pct_loss`; help on all six pages; the tuners vignette; NEWS; DESIGN's orchestration line.

Tracking: `cairn/milestones/M69-selection-rule.md`.

title: M70: nested_fit_resamples() scores a fixed workflow on the outer folds; the five orchestrators refuse one
description:
## Summary

M70: a sixth orchestrator, `nested_fit_resamples()`, scores a workflow with nothing to tune on the outer folds of a nested design. It shares the outer loop with the five tuning orchestrators and skips the inner stage, so a fixed workflow and a tuned one run on identical outer folds and their per-fold metrics join by fold label. Its record names the tuner `fit_resamples` with no `grid`, `param_info` or `select`; every reader answers on it; `nested_final_fit()` fits the workflow as given on every row.

The five tuning orchestrators now refuse a workflow with no `tune()` marker at entry (`nestedtune_untuned_workflow`), naming the new export; `nested_fit_resamples()` refuses a marked workflow (`nestedtune_tuned_workflow`).

Tracking: `cairn/milestones/M70-fit-resamples.md`; decision D-057.

Note: `man/nestedtune-package.Rd` gains the hex-logo line, a `document()` catch-up from the branch point rather than M70 work.

title: M71: `nested_workflow_map()` runs a `workflow_set` through one nested design
description:
## M71: `nested_workflow_map()` runs a `workflow_set` through one nested design

Score every workflow of a `workflow_set` on the same outer folds of one nested design in one call.

- `nested_workflow_map(object, fn = "nested_tune_grid", ...)`: runs each workflow of the set in order through the named orchestrator, routing an unmarked workflow to `nested_fit_resamples()`, merging each workflow's `option` entry over `...`, narrowing the arguments to the routed orchestrator's formals, and reinstating the generator state before each workflow so every workflow runs under the same per-fold seeds.
- A standalone `nested_results_set` class (`wflow_id`, `workflow`, `result`) with the six `collect_*` readers stacking per-element tables under `wflow_id`, `print()`, and `extract_workflow(x, id)`.
- `nested_final_fit(object, results, ..., id = NULL)` reads a workflow and its record from the set by `id`.
- Entry refusals for the set, `fn`, `...` names, `option` names, fitted or wrongly-marked workflows, and missing packages.
- `workflowsets` in Suggests (D-058); help, pkgdown, NEWS, DESIGN, a `tuners.Rmd` section and an `estimate.Rmd` paragraph.

Milestone file: `cairn/milestones/M71-workflow-map.md`.

title: M62: a vignette reads the results object
description:
Ships `vignettes/results.Rmd` ("Reading the results"): the columns of a `nested_results`, `summary()`, `collect_metrics()` both ways, `agreement()`, both `autoplot()` views, a run with one planted failing fold and the partial-summary warning, the dplyr verbs that keep the class and the ones that shed it, and `eval_time` on a censored-regression run. Adds the page under Guides in `_pkgdown.yml` and a NEWS entry.

Milestone file: `cairn/milestones/M062-results-vignette.md`.

title: M63: a site-only article runs the outer loop on mirai daemons
description:
Ships `vignettes/articles/parallel.Rmd` ("Running the outer loop in parallel"), a pkgdown-only article that starts two mirai daemons, runs the getting-started guide's loop on them, shows the result identical to the serial run, and walks the pre-flight, the wire, the `load_all()` caveat, interrupting, and the dispatcher warning. Adds the `Articles` section to `_pkgdown.yml` and a NEWS entry.

Milestone file: `cairn/milestones/M063-parallel-article.md`.

title: M64: site-only article repeats a null-data simulation showing tuned-CV optimism and the nested estimate removing it
description: Adds `vignettes/articles/why-nest.Rmd` ("Why nest: a simulation"), a site-only article built by pkgdown from a committed store (`vignettes/articles/why-nest.rds`) that `vignettes/articles/why-nest-sim.R` produces: 30 seeded replicates of pure-noise wide data (n = 60, p = 200, fair-coin label), a `parsnip::mlp()` on the `nnet` engine tuned over a 20-candidate grid, the flat `tune_grid()` best accuracy against `nested_tune_grid()`'s estimate. The article reads every design figure, both medians and the provenance from the store. `_pkgdown.yml` lists the article; NEWS carries the entry. `nnet` is not declared in DESCRIPTION (D-051). Tracking: M64 milestone file, D-050/D-051, RB06/RR06 archived.

title: M65: collect_notes(), collect_selections() and collect_inner_metrics() on nested_results
description:
Three readers stack a per-fold list column of a `nested_results` into one table with the recorded fold labels beside it: `collect_notes()` (a method on tune's generic, re-exported), `collect_selections()` and `collect_inner_metrics()` (package-owned generics with aborting defaults). The two stackers read completed folds only, warn once on a partial run and refuse an all-failed run, the rule `collect_metrics()` and `agreement()` share.

Milestone file: `cairn/milestones/M65-collect-readers.md`.

title: M66: vignette pages read through the readers under library(tidymodels), prose pass
description:
The six pages under `vignettes/` read the results through `collect_selections()`, `collect_notes()` and `collect_inner_metrics()`, dplyr verbs and `tibble()`, with `library(tidymodels)` attached before `library(nestedtune)` behind a guard. `tidymodels` joins Suggests. The final fit's tuning run is reached through `extract_tune_results()` and `show_best()`. A prose pass over all six pages with every finding dispositioned in the milestone file. Two `benchmarks/` scripts: the idiom, prefix and prose sweep, and the vignette timing script. NEWS entry.

Milestone file: `cairn/milestones/M66-vignette-sweep.md`.

title: M67: extract_procedure() on both objects; em dashes leave user-facing text
description:
Adds \`extract_procedure()\`, a package-owned S3 generic with methods on \`nested_results\` (the \`procedure\` attribute) and \`nested_final_fit\` (the \`procedure\` slot) and a default that aborts as \`nestedtune_no_extract_method\`. Every roxygen and vignette site that reached the record by hand now names the accessor. The results print's candidates line drops its em dash, and the em dashes leave the help pages, \`_pkgdown.yml\`, \`NEWS.md\`, \`README.Rmd\` and the re-knit \`README.md\`.

Milestone file: \`cairn/milestones/M67-extract-procedure.md\`.

title: M56: the results class, the extract defaults and the final-fit page close the M37, M34 and M51 review findings
description:
M56: the results class, the extract defaults and the final-fit page close the M37, M34 and M51 review findings.

- `print.nested_results()` returns after the rows on the columnless type token `vctrs::vec_cbind_frame_ptype()` hands back, emitting neither the outer-label line nor a fold count.
- A column add that duplicates a record column's name under `.name_repair = "minimal"` sheds the class through both doors (`vec_restore()` and `can_reconstruct_results()`).
- `names<-.nested_results()` keeps the object and its attributes intact when every record column keeps its name; a moved or duplicated record name sheds them.
- The `extract_` default methods refuse an object with no method before any dots check.
- The `?nested_final_fit` reproducibility recipe carries a racing and an annealing branch; the racing and annealing pages date the `workflow_size` classification to finetune 1.3.0.
- NEWS entries for the above.

Milestone record: `cairn/milestones/M056-results-class-and-help-page-findings.md`.

title: M57: the hang trace, the parallel-files setup and two test files close the M52, M37 and M34 review findings
description:
Closes the review findings on the hang trace, the parallel-files setup, `test-vctrs-compat.R` and `test-dots-barrier.R` that the M52, M37 and M34 reviews deferred.

- A test forbids duplicate `test_that()` descriptions within any test file, and another resolves every `Config/testthat/start-first` name to a file.
- `HangTraceReporter$end_file()` prunes `open` as well as `seen`; the two hang-trace tempdir leaks are closed.
- The fixture-cache teardown report goes to `stderr()`, and its comments say the cache is per worker process.
- `R-CMD-check-hard.yaml` caps its job at 30 minutes and sets `TESTTHAT_CPUS`; PROFILE names the capped workflows.
- Every `tibble::`-calling block in `test-vctrs-compat.R` opens with the tibble skip.
- The dots-barrier registry probe names the methods it must reach; the `collect_metrics(` source scan is removed for a runtime refusal test.

Milestone file: `cairn/milestones/M057-test-suite-and-ci-findings.md`.

title: M58: the startup check asks every daemon for each package the workflow and the tuner need, and the host's entry check reads the same list
description:
The parallel pre-flight sends every daemon the package list the attach step already builds (the workflow's `required_pkgs()` plus the tuner's own requirements) and each daemon reports which it cannot load. A pool with a daemon lacking a package is refused before any fold is dispatched, under the new class `nestedtune_daemons_missing_pkgs` (also `nestedtune_daemons_unusable`), naming the daemons, the packages and the install-then-restart remedy. `preflight_outcome()` gains the `missing_pkgs` rung between `cannot_load` and `incompatible`.

The host's entry check widens from the engine's packages to the workflow's (`check_workflow_pkgs()` replaces `check_model_spec()`), refusing under `nestedtune_pkg_not_installed` with an install hint, across the five tuning drivers and `nested_final_fit()`.

One helper (`needed_pkgs()` / `workflow_pkgs()`) builds the list for the probe, the attach step and the host.

Tracking: cairn/milestones/M58-preflight-workflow-pkgs.md

title: M59: every driver refuses inner splits that are not rsplits, sit on a foreign frame, or index rows the outer fold holds out
description:
`check_nested()` gains three rules, run last: every element of a fold's inner `splits` list is an `rsplit`; a fold's inner splits all carry one frame identical to the outer split's frame or its analysis set; a whole-frame inner split's `in_id` and non-`NA` `out_id` index only rows inside the outer split's `in_id`. All five tuning drivers refuse at the call under `nestedtune_bad_design`, naming every offending fold, split and index, with no frame interpolated into the message.

The suite's failure fixtures (`break_fold()`, `break_inner_split()`) are re-vehicled inside the design's own frame. `@param resamples`, NEWS and the `R/parallel.R` fat-path comment are updated; D-049 supersedes D-047's consequence clause.

Tracking: `cairn/milestones/M59-inner-split-frame-checks.md`.

title: M60: the guide splits into a getting-started path and a page on what the estimate means; the citation guard sweeps every page under vignettes/
description:
Splits `vignettes/nested-cv.Rmd` into a short getting-started guide (design, loop, report, final fit, reproducibility, write-up) and a new code-free page `vignettes/estimate.Rmd` on what the estimate means, carrying the estimand, pessimism and `std_err` material, the no-comparison warning, the disagreement mechanism, when nesting is worth its cost, the feature-selection caveat and the References.

The citation guard in `tests/testthat/test-vignette-citations.R` now enumerates every `.Rmd` under `vignettes/` recursively, applies its References rules per page, and adds a prose-numeral rule: every paragraph containing a digit (outside code, backtick spans, YAML and References) must carry an author-year citation. Each rule is shown red on planted fixtures.

Also: `estimate` listed under Guides in `_pkgdown.yml`, `^vignettes/articles$` in `.Rbuildignore`, README links both pages, NEWS entry.

Milestone file: `cairn/milestones/M060-guide-split.md`.

title: M61: a vignette runs the four alternative inner tuners on one design
description:
Adds \`vignettes/tuners.Rmd\` ("Choosing the inner tuner"): runs \`nested_tune_bayes()\`, \`nested_tune_race_anova()\`, \`nested_tune_race_win_loss()\` and \`nested_tune_sim_anneal()\` on the getting-started guide's design and workflow, prints one fold's \`.inner_metrics\` for each, passes a \`tune::control_bayes()\` through \`...\` and reads the recorded \`procedure\`, and says what differs from calling tune or finetune directly.

The racing and annealing sections build only where finetune, lme4 and BradleyTerry2 are installed; the page exits with a notice when ranger is absent. Adds the page under Guides in \`_pkgdown.yml\` and a NEWS entry.

Milestone record: \`cairn/milestones/M061-tuner-vignette.md\`.

title: M51: nested_tune_sim_anneal() runs finetune's simulated annealing inside the outer loop
description:
Adds `nested_tune_sim_anneal()`, a sibling of `nested_tune_bayes()` that runs `finetune::tune_sim_anneal()` inside each outer fold: a `tune_sim_anneal` registry entry, `iter` and `initial` as its own arguments (floors 1 and 1, D-046), `.iter` on each fold's `.inner_metrics`, the final fit re-running an annealing search, and a help page classifying every `control_sim_anneal()` slot.

Closes #35

title: M52: the test suite runs its files in parallel
description:
Test files run in parallel (`Config/testthat/parallel: true`), the eleven slowest queued first, with one worker per runner core set through `TESTTHAT_CPUS` in both gating workflows. The hang trace keeps one live start/end pair per file and block under parallel files, so a job killed at its cap still names the block it died in. The benchmark profiler pins itself serial.

Milestone file: `cairn/milestones/M52-parallel-test-files.md`.

title: M53: nested_final_fit() refuses a results object whose every outer fold failed
description:
\`nested_final_fit()\` refuses a \`nested_results\` whose \`.completed\` column is all \`FALSE\`, with condition class \`nestedtune_no_completed_folds\`, immediately after the three record refusals and before the tuner, grid and seed steps. The same class goes on \`check_any_completed()\`, so \`collect_metrics()\`, \`autoplot()\` and \`agreement()\` on such an object signal one class. Help pages of the four doors name the class; NEWS carries one entry.

Tracking: \`cairn/milestones/M53-final-fit-all-failed.md\`.

title: M54: inner tuning finalizes an unknown parameter range on the outer fold's analysis rows
description:
## Summary

- Before each fold's inner tuning call, the inner rset is reframed on the outer split's analysis rows (`analysis_framed_inner()` in `R/nested-resamples.R`), so tune's own finalization of an unknown parameter range (`min_n`, `mtry`, ...) never sees the outer assessment rows.
- Applies only when every inner split carries the outer split's whole frame and the outer `in_id` has no repeats; an `rsample::nested_cv()` design or a repeated-index `manual_rset()` outer split reaches `run_tuner()` untouched.
- Roxygen on the three `@param param_info` sites and `?nested_final_fit`'s `@param results` name the finalization frame; DESIGN.md names the rebuild as the GP1 divergence; one NEWS entry.
- New test file `tests/testthat/test-nested-tune-finalize.R` (105 expectations): frame identity per tuner over the registry, candidate bounds against the fold's analysis-row count, `identical()` results against the `rsample::nested_cv()` design, and untouched-design pass-through.

Milestone file: `cairn/milestones/M54-inner-finalize-analysis-frame.md`.

title: M55: every driver refuses a malformed nested design at entry
description:
The five orchestrators (`nested_tune_grid()`, `nested_tune_bayes()`, `nested_tune_race_anova()`, `nested_tune_race_win_loss()`, `nested_tune_sim_anneal()`) refuse, before any fold runs, a nested design whose inner `rset` has no rows, whose label columns hold an `NA` or a repeated label tuple, or whose label columns are not named `id`/`id[1-9]` and character or factor. Every design refusal `check_nested()` raises now carries the class `nestedtune_bad_design`, the exported driver's call, and every offending position or column.

- `R/checks.R`: `check_inner_rows()`, `check_label_columns()`, `check_label_values()`; `check_column_class()` names every offending element.
- Tests: `malformed_designs()` fixture (25 planted designs) and one block per driver.
- `@param resamples` documents the contract; `NEWS.md` entry.

Milestone file: `cairn/milestones/M55-design-entry-checks.md`.

title: M45: the inner loop takes its tuner as an argument, and nested_tune_bayes() is its second consumer
description:
## Summary

- The outer loop takes its tuner as an argument: an internal tuner description (`R/tuner.R`) names the tune function and its static arguments, and is threaded through `nested_fold_fit()`, `dispatch_folds()`, the mirai lean task, `fold_task()` and `final_fit_worker()` in place of the `grid` formal. The loop body shared by both orchestrators lives in `nested_loop()`.
- `nested_tune_bayes()` is exported: nested cross-validation around `tune::tune_bayes()` with `iter`, `initial` and `objective` as its own arguments; `control_bayes()` is built inside the fold's seed scope with the fold's tuning seed. Entry checks refuse a bad `iter`, `initial` (a `tune_results` included) or `objective` before any fitting.
- Every result records a `procedure` attribute naming the tuner and its static arguments; the per-fold candidate record carries `.iter`.
- Oracles: a hand-rolled reference loop on two fixtures, the `iter = 0` identity with `nested_tune_grid()`, the eight RNG properties, and serial-versus-daemon identity at two daemon counts. The grid path's numbers are identical before and after.
- Docs: help page with a "Differences from calling tune directly" section, pkgdown row, NEWS, DESIGN.

Tracking: `cairn/milestones/M45-nested-tune-bayes.md`.

Refs #35

title: M46: nested_final_fit() re-runs the procedure a result recorded
description:
`nested_final_fit()` now takes the workflow and the `nested_results` whose estimate the user will report, and re-runs the procedure that object recorded — grid or Bayesian — over the full data.

- Both orchestrators record the design's `inside` call on every `nested_results` as an `inside` attribute, carried through `run_attributes()`.
- `nested_final_fit(object, results, ...)`: the inner specification, the data and the procedure are read from the results object. A results object with no record, or with no rows, is refused under one condition class. The former `grid`, `param_info`, `metrics`, `event_level` and `eval_time` formals are gone (pre-1.0, no deprecation cycle).
- The Bayesian final-fit path goes through the tuner description; oracles, RNG and read-nothing-but-splits tests cover it.
- `print()` and `summary()` name the procedure for both tuners; `extract_scored_candidates()` works on a Bayesian final fit.
- Docs, NEWS, DESIGN and the vignette's final-fit section updated.

Milestone: cairn/milestones/M46-final-fit-recorded-procedure.md

title: M47: predict() and augment() on a nested_final_fit
description:
Adds `predict()` and `augment()` methods on the object `nested_final_fit()` returns, each delegating to the trained workflow inside it, and re-exports `augment` beside `collect_metrics()`.

- `predict.nested_final_fit()` forwards `...` to the workflow, where parsnip refuses unknown names.
- `augment.nested_final_fit()` fences its dots with `check_dots_empty()`, since workflows' method ignores them.
- One help page for both, carrying the caveat that augmenting the training rows gives in-sample residuals, not this model's performance.
- pkgdown row, NEWS entry, README and vignette switched to the direct call, DESIGN lines updated.
- Tests on the regression, classification and censored-regression fixtures; the metric-generic refusals asserted still standing.

Tracking: `cairn/milestones/M47-final-fit-predict-augment.md`.

title: M48: `control` reaches the inner tuning call through `...`, and every control slot is documented
description:
`control = tune::control_grid(...)` / `tune::control_bayes(...)` passed through `...` on `nested_tune_grid()` and `nested_tune_bayes()` now reaches the inner tuning call in every fold and in the final fit. `...` accepts `control` and nothing else; forced slots (`allow_par = FALSE`, the fold's tuning seed as the Bayesian `seed`, `event_level` from the argument) overwrite the caller's, a conflicting `event_level` is refused. The `procedure` attribute records the effective control, and both help pages classify every `control_grid()` / `control_bayes()` slot under one of six headings (forced, settable as its own argument, refused, passed through, not returned, inert).

Tracking: `cairn/milestones/M48-dots-control-passthrough.md`.

Closes #33
Refs #35

title: M49: each outer fold keeps its inner search's metrics as .inner_metrics in place of .grid
description:
Each outer fold of a `nested_results` now keeps its inner tuning run's `tune::collect_metrics()` table in a `.inner_metrics` list column, replacing `.grid`. The Bayesian table carries `.iter`. A fold that tuned and then failed its outer fit keeps its table; a fold that scored nothing carries a zero-row table with a completed fold's columns. `.selected` is unchanged.

The print and summary candidate-set comparison now derives each fold's candidate set from the distinct parameter rows of `.inner_metrics`. `.inner_metrics` joins the dplyr/vctrs invariant column set and `has_results_columns()`. `extract_scored_candidates()` on a final fit keeps its shape.

Tracking: cairn/milestones/M49-inner-metrics-column.md, D-043.

Closes #57

title: M50: nested_tune_race_anova() and nested_tune_race_win_loss() run finetune's racing tuners inside the outer loop
description:
Two new exports, `nested_tune_race_anova()` and `nested_tune_race_win_loss()`, run finetune's racing tuners inside the outer loop with `nested_tune_grid()`'s arguments and a `finetune::control_race()` through `...`. Each fold's `.inner_metrics` records every candidate the race scored (`all_configs = TRUE`) with `n` the resamples it was scored on. Entry refusals: finetune / lme4 / BradleyTerry2 absent, a control of another class, an inner design no larger than `burn_in`. `nested_final_fit()` re-runs the race on the full data. A tuner registry in `R/tuner.R` replaces the per-tuner `switch()`es. finetune, lme4 and BradleyTerry2 join Suggests (D-044).

Tracking: `cairn/milestones/M50-finetune-racing.md`.

Refs #35

title: A results object's own fold-label columns, recorded rather than guessed
description:
`nested_results` now reads its fold-label columns off a record the constructor
wrote, instead of matching `^id[0-9]*$` against the object's current names. A
column a caller adds is read as a fold label only when the resampling design
itself carried a column of that name.

- `new_nested_results()` records `setdiff(names(resamples), c("splits", "inner_resamples"))`
  as an attribute; it travels in `run_attributes()`, so `stamp_results()` and
  `copy_results_attributes()` carry it and `bare_results()` strips it.
- `id_columns()`, `record_columns()`, `has_results_columns()`, `fold_ids()`,
  `can_reconstruct_results()` and `template_record()` read that record.
- `can_reconstruct_results()` refuses rather than aborts when a recorded label
  column cannot be ordered.
- `NEWS.md` and the `@return` say what the code now does.

Milestone: `cairn/milestones/M38-id-columns-recorded.md`

title: Attach the workflow's packages in every mirai daemon
description:
Fixes #37.

## What was wrong

A recipe selector written unqualified — `all_numeric_predictors()`, as in the reprex on #37 — is a quosure resolved through the search path. A `mirai` daemon's search path carries base R and nothing else.

`tune` loads a workflow's `required_pkgs()` as *namespaces* and only *attaches* them on its own parallel path: `attach_pkgs()` is a no-op whenever the strategy is sequential (tune 2.1.0). The inner tuning run here is sequential by construction — `control_grid(allow_par = FALSE)`, because nested parallelism oversubscribes cores — so nothing attached anything inside the daemon running the fold. The same call ran clean serially off the caller's own attached packages, which is what made this look like a parallel-only quirk.

The daemon pre-flight could not have caught it. It asks whether a daemon holds *this* package; it never asks what the workflow needs.

## The fix

`dispatch_folds()` calls `attach_daemon_pkgs()` after the pre-flight and before the first fold is sent: one `mirai::everywhere()` round trip that runs `library()` for each of `tune::required_pkgs(object)` in every daemon, bounded by the same deadline-poll the pre-flight uses. A package that will not attach is reported in a warning rather than raised on — the fold that needs it fails with tune's own message naming the function it could not find, which says more.

Nothing attaches in the caller's own session: serially the search path is already whatever the caller made it, and it is not ours to change.

## Regression test

`tests/testthat/test-parallel-required-pkgs.R`, one test, two daemons. Every recipe fixture in the suite qualifies its selectors (`recipes::all_predictors()`), which is why nothing here reproduced the bug — the new fixture leaves the selector bare.

It asks every daemon whether `recipes` is on its search path before and after the run, so the assertion pins *which* mechanism made the fold succeed: absent beforehand, present afterwards.

Against the parent commit:

```
── Failure ('test-parallel-required-pkgs.R:66:3')
Expected `all(res$.completed)` to be TRUE.  actual: FALSE
── Failure ('test-parallel-required-pkgs.R:67:3')
Expected `all(attached())` to be TRUE.      actual: FALSE
```

with the fold notes reading `could not find function "all_predictors"`. Passing on this branch. Full suite green.

The file is registered in the time-budget ledger (one pool start, one bounded read at an explicit 30 s) and added to `BUDGETED_FILES`.

title: M01: memory-lean nested resampling structure
description:
Ships `nestedtune` as an installable R package with one export,
`nested_resamples(data, outside, inside)`.

It builds the same nested resampling design as `rsample::nested_cv()` —
identical splits for the same seed, down to the attributes of the retrieved
frames — without keeping a materialized analysis frame per outer fold. On
`mlbench::LetterRecognition` (20000 × 17) with five inner folds, as multiples
of the source data size:

| outer folds | `rsample::nested_cv()` | `nested_resamples()` |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 2.2× | 1.2× |
| 5 | 5.6× | 1.7× |
| 10 | 11.4× | 2.6× |
| 50 | 57.5× | 10.0× |

The remaining growth is index vectors, which rsample stores too; the copies of
the data are gone. This is the cause diagnosed in rsample#283 —
`inside_resample()` calls `as.data.frame(src)`.

The returned object carries rsample's `nested_cv` class and spec attributes,
and inner resamples keep their own class, `id` columns (including `id2`), and
attributes, so it is a drop-in substitution.

## Verification

- `devtools::test()`: 476 passing, 0 failures
- `devtools::check()`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
- `devtools::document()`: no diff · `pkgdown::check_pkgdown()`: clean

Three independent oracle types back the size claim: **live** (rsample
recomputed at test time), **closed-form** (an analytic storage model predicting
every measured size within 0.72%, against a 2% tolerance), plus a negative
control asserting the model does *not* fit rsample's sizes.

## Deliberate divergence from rsample

An outer bootstrap is refused rather than warned about — the same observation
can otherwise land in both the inner analysis and inner assessment set. rsample
inspects only the deparsed call, so a namespaced call or a prebuilt object
slips past its warning; both are caught here.

title: Outer-loop orchestration: nested_tune_grid()
description:
Runs the nested cross-validation loop end to end.

`nested_tune_grid()` takes a workflow and a nested resampling design and drives
the outer loop: for each outer fold it tunes on that fold's inner resamples with
`tune::tune_grid()`, selects, finalizes, and fits and scores on the held-out
outer split with `last_fit()`. Every statistical step is delegated to tune; what
this adds is the loop, a reproducibility contract, and a results object that
keeps each fold's *chosen parameters* alongside its metrics — so disagreement
between folds is visible rather than averaged away.

`collect_metrics()` returns either the per-fold numbers or the nested estimate.

## Reproducibility

One `set.seed()` before the call fixes the result. The function draws two seeds
per outer fold up front, assigns them by fold position, applies them with the
generator kind pinned, and restores the caller's RNG state on exit including on
error. A fold's result therefore depends on its position in the design, not on
the order folds run in — which is what makes the loop safe to parallelize later.

The scheme was settled by an independent review (RR01), which verified against
tune 2.1.0 that tune >= 2.0.0 already derives its own per-resample L'Ecuyer
substreams even when running sequentially, and is net-zero on the caller's RNG
state. That finding is why `tune (>= 2.0.0)` is pinned rather than left open.

## Verification

Two independent oracle types back the nested estimate: a live reference
implementation (a hand-rolled `tune_grid()` -> `select_best()` ->
`finalize_workflow()` -> `last_fit()` loop, written from the documented seed
contract rather than from the driver) and an invariant (with a single-candidate
grid there is nothing to select, so per-fold metrics must equal
`tune::fit_resamples()` on the same outer rset).

Leakage is checked rather than asserted: the driver's per-fold handoff is
instrumented, so a split/inner mis-pairing — which would leave every individual
object valid — is caught.

702 tests pass; `devtools::check()` is clean at 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.

title: M03: fold failures are recorded, never fatal
description:
A failing outer fold no longer ends the run. The remaining folds still run, and the failed one is recorded rather than discarded.

## What changed

- `nested_fold_fit()` returns an outcome record instead of throwing. Both stages are wrapped, and both quiet failure paths are caught: inner tuning raises only at `select_best()` after `tune_grid()` has already returned with a warning, and `last_fit()` never raises at all — it hands back a result whose metrics are `NULL`.
- tune's own notes are carried through verbatim, beside a note naming the failing stage.
- `nested_results` gains `.notes` and `.completed` columns plus `folds_attempted` / `folds_completed` attributes.
- `collect_metrics()` summarizes only completed folds, warns naming the rest, and aborts when none completed.
- `check_grid_params()` refuses a malformed data-frame `grid` before any fitting, in both directions.

## Principles

IP4 (the estimate describes the design actually executed), IP2 (fold seeds unaffected by a neighbour's failure), GP1 (tune's notes idiom and its end-of-run warning mirrored), GP3 (a provably invalid grid refused, not warned about).

title: Parallel outer folds
description:
`nested_tune_grid()` now runs its outer folds concurrently on mirai daemons, producing results identical to a serial run.

Start workers with `mirai::daemons(n)` before the call and the loop uses them; there is no argument to set, and no daemons means the serial behaviour is unchanged. Inner tuning stays serial.

## Reproducibility (IP2)

Every parallel run in the test suite and the benchmark came back `identical()` to its serial counterpart — at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 daemons, under a caller-set non-default generator kind, and on daemons deliberately polluted with a different RNG kind triple, consumed draws, a prior fold's residue, and shadowing globals.

The seeding scheme is unchanged: D-011's seeds are drawn at entry and assigned by fold position, with the generator kind pinned per fold. RR03 verified by execution that the kind pin is load-bearing rather than precautionary — mirai starts every daemon on its own L'Ecuyer-CMRG stream, so without the pin a worker would draw from a different generator than the serial run.

## Checks

- `devtools::check()` — 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
- `devtools::check()` under `_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_=true` (CRAN's noSuggests flavour) — 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
- Test suite: 1026 passing, 0 failures, 0 warnings

## Performance

52.6s serial to 18.6s on 6 warm daemons (2.83x) on a 6x5 design with ranger. Near-linear at 2 daemons, falling off after; `benchmarks/parallel-speedup.R` reproduces the figures. No test asserts a speedup.

Driven by review brief RB03 / report RR03, whose nine binding criteria are ingested verbatim as acceptance criteria; two deviations are recorded in the milestone file.

title: Selection instability you can see
description:

The default view puts one point per outer fold at the value that fold's inner

uses so the figure and the summary cannot disagree. Its subtitle carries IP3's
caveat where ggplot2 renders it into the image, so it survives export into a

Both views keep every *attempted* fold on the axis: a fold that failed, or one
that completed without a value for a parameter, leaves a visible gap rather than

title: A stopped run reports nothing, not a partial estimate
description:
Cancelling a parallel run made it report a number for a design that never
executed. `mirai::stop_mirai()` resolves every outstanding task to a bare
`errorValue` carrying none of the interrupt classes, so those tasks fell
through to `failed_fold()` — folds that were never given a chance to run were
recorded as folds that had been attempted and failed, and the run completed
normally over whatever had finished. That is the IP4 inversion the interrupt
branch exists to prevent, reached by a route it never saw.

`classify_fold_result()` now aborts on it with `nestedtune_cancelled`, which
inherits `nestedtune_interrupted` so existing handlers keep working. The
caller's RNG state is restored by the same `on.exit()` as every other abort.

## The boundary this could not cross

T1 probed every teardown path by execution rather than trusting the plan's
premise, and found the plan wrong on one point. `stop_mirai()` is code 20 and
unambiguous. But `daemons(0)` with folds outstanding yields code **19 — the
same value, with the same classes, that a daemon dying mid-fold yields**, and
M07 verified that case *is* a genuine fold failure. Nothing in the returned
value separates them.

So 19 keeps its existing behaviour and the limit is documented rather than
guessed at. Aborting on it would discard every completed fold whenever one
worker died — exactly what the failed-fold handling exists to prevent. The
milestone's scope and two acceptance criteria were amended at a gate to say so.

## A defect found by the inversion pass

R coerces across types in `==`, so a worker error whose message is the string
`"20"` compares equal to the cancel code. Without the `is.integer()` shape
check, one unlucky error message would abort the run and throw away every
completed fold. Pinned by its own test.

## Verification

- 1115 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip
- `devtools::check()` 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
- Both new guards proven red by inversion

title: The startup check inspects every worker and says what went wrong
description:
The pre-flight check before parallel dispatch now reaches every connected
daemon, and distinguishes a daemon that cannot load the package from one
that did not answer in time.

**Two defects fixed.** The probe submitted a single `mirai::mirai()` task,
which one daemon takes — so in a heterogeneous pool (a respawned daemon,
differing library paths) one loadable daemon passed the check for all of
them and the rest returned opaque per-fold worker failures. And its one
message covered two different outcomes, so a timeout was reported with
install-and-prime remedies: telling a user to install what they already
have.

**Now.** `daemons_load_status()` asks every daemon via `mirai::everywhere()`
and classifies each answer as loaded / cannot load / no answer. A load
failure keeps the install-and-prime remedies; a non-response gets its own
message and class; a pool failing both ways names both counts. Both carry a
shared `nestedtune_daemons_unusable`, so a handler that only cares the check
failed catches either, and code written against `nestedtune_daemons_cannot_load`
keeps working.

**The bound** moves from a hard-coded 30 s to
`options(nestedtune.preflight_timeout = <ms>)`, validated and refusing `Inf`
— an unbounded wait is not a bound. `nested_tune_grid()`'s formals are pinned
literally so the signature cannot grow the argument D-018 refused.

**One consequence, documented rather than absorbed.** Waiting for every
daemon means the first call against a cold pool waits for the slowest cold
load, not for whichever daemon was free. On a loaded machine that can exceed
the 30 s default; the default is held and the cost is documented where users
meet it.

`devtools::test()` 1164 passing / 0 failures / 0 skips.
`devtools::check()` Status: OK (0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes).

title: Every CI run is one somebody is waiting for
description:
Both GitHub Actions workflows gain two changes:

- **`concurrency`** — a run is cancelled once a later push supersedes it, on
  every ref except the default branch. `main` is a distribution channel, so a
  commit there keeps a completed check rather than a cancelled one.
- **`paths-ignore`** — commits touching only `cairn/**`, `CLAUDE.md`, or
  `.claude/**` fire no run. They cannot change what `R CMD check` sees.

Measured over `[2026-07-26T00:00Z, 2026-07-27T07:00Z)`, these remove 39 of 108
runs and 877 of 2,276 machine-minutes. `.github/ci-usage.py` reproduces that
measurement — reading the path filter out of the workflow files rather than
restating it — and `.github/ci-usage-baseline.md` is its committed output.
